title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Birmingham, AL: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Birmingham steel, pipe, power and structural welders: D1.1, ASME or API 1104 for Part C. Corporate, online or one-to-one.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Birmingham, Alabama: Six Days for Steel, Pipe, Power and Structural Welding Inspectors
html:
Birmingham grew up on iron and steel, and welding still runs through its economy: electric arc furnace steel and seamless tube in Fairfield, a bar mill, a pipe maker owned in trust for its employees, the headquarters of the company that operates the Farley, Hatch and Vogtle nuclear plants, and general contractors that sit at the top of national rankings. Wherever welded steel is built or repaired to a code, somebody has to inspect it, and the qualification owners and contractors ask for most often is the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI).

Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for that examination with a six-day (6-day) course covering Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. It is available as corporate delivery at an employer's facility, as online study, or as one-to-one sessions with the instructor. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification; Atlantis certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in Birmingham, as the company's offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. To talk through the options, send a Birmingham CWI enquiry.

How the six days work for a Birmingham candidate

The six days follow the structure of the exam. Day one builds vocabulary and symbol reading: arc welding processes, oxyfuel cutting, AWS terms, joint types and the welding symbol system. Day two covers metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuities and their causes, what each NDT method can and cannot find, safety, fabrication math and inspector ethics. Day three rehearses the practical with real gauges and welds, day four is spent working through the code book you choose for Part C, day five is timed practice papers, and day six revisits weak areas and the logistics of the AWS application. The full breakdown is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

  • Corporate: a steel mill contractor, pipe maker, structural fabricator or outage contractor preparing a group has the six days delivered at its own facility, using its welds, gauges and, where it fits, its code and procedures.
  • Online: an individual follows a study plan built on the six-day outline, with course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and puts questions to an instructor while working. There are no scheduled class times; the candidate sets the pace.
  • One-to-one: one candidate takes six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

Atlantis writes the practice questions itself from the AWS topic lists; they are not real AWS examination questions. AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

Birmingham's welding economy, sector by sector

Steel mills and tubular products

U.S. Steel's Fairfield Works started up an electric arc furnace in 2020 to supply its tubular operations, and in September 2026 the company broke ground on a quench and tempering facility at Fairfield Tubular Operations. Nucor runs a steel bar mill in Birmingham. Mills like these need welding inspection twice over: for new process equipment, structures and supports during projects, and for the endless repair of cranes, ladles, rolls, chutes and material handling equipment between them. TASSCO, a supplier of abrasion- and impact-resistant material handling products, hosted the AWS Birmingham Section for a meeting and shop tour in February 2025, a reminder that wear-resistant fabrication and hardfacing are part of the local trade.

Pipe

American Cast Iron Pipe Company (ACIPCO), headquartered in Birmingham and held in trust for its employees under its founder's will, makes ductile iron pipe for waterworks along with hydrants, valves and fire pumps. Its product lines also include spiral-welded steel pipe for water transmission and high-frequency-welded steel pipe for the energy industry, made at plants in several states. Welded pipe manufacturing brings mill-side quality work, from procedure control to seam inspection and testing to product specifications, and the contractors who lay that pipe need field inspectors who know API 1104 or the waterworks standards.

Power generation and nuclear

Southern Nuclear, headquartered in Birmingham, operates six reactors at three plants: Farley in Alabama, and Hatch and Vogtle in Georgia. Nuclear welding is governed by the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, with construction rules in Section III, repair and replacement under Section XI, and procedures and welders qualified to Section IX, all inside a quality assurance program that leaves no room for undocumented work. Refueling outages concentrate maintenance and modification welding into short windows, and the supply chain feeding the fleet, from component fabricators to outage contractors, needs inspectors who are comfortable working inside that documentation. Fossil and gas generating plants across the state add boiler tube, steam piping and structural repair work under ASME B31.1 and AWS D1.1.

Construction contractors and structural steel

Birmingham is home to several of the country's large general contractors. In the Associated Builders and Contractors' 2026 Top Performers lists, BL Harbert ranked first nationally in government, hospitality and sports complexes, Brasfield & Gorrie first in office, and Robins & Morton first in health care. Their projects across the Southeast use a great deal of structural steel welded to AWS D1.1, checked by fabricators' QC staff and, on larger buildings, by special inspectors working under the building code. Steel fabricators and erectors around the city supply much of that work.

Bridges, highways and manufacturing

State highway work around Birmingham's interstate junctions brings bridge steel fabricated under AWS D1.5, with inspection in the shop and in the field. Across central Alabama, automotive plants and their suppliers, truck body and equipment builders, and general fabrication shops employ welding inspectors too, mostly working to D1.1 or to customer specifications.

Who hires CWIs around Birmingham

  • Steel mills, pipe makers and their contractors. QC and maintenance departments want inspectors who can check repair procedures, preheat and hardfacing as well as new structural welds.
  • Structural steel fabricators and erectors. Shops supplying the region's building contractors need in-house CWIs to accept work to D1.1 before it ships.
  • Testing labs and special inspection firms. Larger building projects require special inspection of structural welding, which is often performed by CWIs.
  • Utility, nuclear and outage contractors. Power plant maintenance and nuclear supply chain work reward inspectors who know ASME Section IX and can live with strict documentation.
  • Bridge fabricators and highway contractors. D1.5 work needs inspectors in the shop and on site.
  • Manufacturers. Equipment and vehicle builders use CWIs to run welding quality programs and audit suppliers.

Choosing the Part C code for Birmingham work

AWS lets you choose the code book for Part C. The options are AWS D1.1 (structural steel), D1.2 (aluminum), D1.5 (bridges), D15.1 (railcars and locomotives), D17.1 (aerospace), API 1104 (pipelines), the ASME package pairing Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. Most Birmingham candidates end up with one of four.

If you mostly work onChooseBecause
Structural steel, mills, fabrication shops, building projectsAWS D1.1It is the code most local structural and maintenance work is done to.
Power plants, nuclear supply chain, process pipingASME packageSection IX qualification with the B31.1 power piping and B31.3 process piping codes.
Pipeline construction and repairAPI 1104Federal pipeline rules incorporate it for welding and weld acceptance.
Highway bridge steelAWS D1.5The bridge welding code for state transportation work.

Nuclear inspectors should note that Section III and Section XI are not Part C books; the ASME package covers Section IX and the piping codes, which is still the closest fit. Study the edition AWS names on your application, not necessarily the newest one. Background: AWS D1.1, the D1.1 weld acceptance criteria guide, ASME Section IX, AWS D1.5 and API 1104.

The AWS Birmingham Section

Birmingham's AWS section belongs to District 9 and runs a steady program. In 2026 it held product demonstration meetings in March and April, including one with Lincoln Electric's Birmingham representative, and in May it met at Jefferson State Community College to hear Kevin E. Bowditch, coauthor of the textbooks Modern Welding and Welding Fundamentals. Section members also reported on the District 9 conference at Auburn University. Jefferson State hosts an AWS student chapter.

For a CWI candidate, the section is where you meet fabricator QC managers, plant welding engineers and experienced inspectors who can tell you which code local employers expect and how they handled the practical. It is also where you find supervisors willing to vouch for your welding history on the AWS application. Meeting details are linked from the section finder on aws.org.

Where Birmingham welders train

Two community colleges anchor the local welding pipeline. Jefferson State Community College runs welding labs at its Clanton, Pell City, Shelby and Jefferson campuses, teaches the NCCER welding curriculum aligned with AWS SENSE entry-level standards, offers certificates and an associate degree, and schedules both day and evening classes. Lawson State Community College teaches welding at its Bessemer campus, with an associate degree in occupational technologies, a certificate and a short certificate; its courses cover shielded metal arc, oxyfuel, gas metal arc and gas tungsten arc welding, use the AWS SENSE and Lincoln Electric NC3 LEEPS programs for stackable credentials, and the program lists an AWS Certified Welding Inspector among its staff.

Completed trade or vocational courses like these can reduce the experience AWS requires, and the transcripts make welding history easier to prove. Neither college has any connection with the Atlantis course; they are mentioned because so many Birmingham welders start there.

Booking the exam from Birmingham

Once AWS accepts your application, the confirmation letter it sends carries the eligibility code you need for Prometric. That code books the two computer-based parts: Part A, 150 fundamentals questions, and Part C, an open-book paper of roughly 50 to 65 questions on your code. AWS states there are more than 100 Prometric centers in the US, so you can choose one convenient to you. Part B is handled separately, because AWS runs the practical itself at its seminar and examination locations, with hands-on tasks using equipment it supplies and 46 questions. Look up the nearest AWS practical session before you set a study timeline; it may involve travel to another city in the Southeast. A score of 72% or more is needed on each part.

Examination and seminar fees are published by AWS on aws.org. Use the CWI exam budget planner to add books, travel and time away from work, and the pass rate by part article to see where to put extra study.

Studying around mill shifts and outage seasons

Steel mills run continuous rotating shifts, and nuclear and fossil plants pack their heaviest maintenance into scheduled outages, typically in the milder spring and fall months when power demand is lower. Construction inspectors, by contrast, work long days in good weather and catch up in winter. None of those patterns fits a weekly class, which is why the online plan has no fixed hours. A practical rhythm: work through fundamentals on your days off, keep your code book at work and use slack time to trace the clauses behind the welds you are inspecting, practise Part B measurements on scrap and test coupons, and keep the timed papers for the final weeks before your Prometric booking. Send questions to the instructor whenever they arise. Candidates who want structure without a class can book one-to-one sessions on the days their rotation allows.

Corporate: six days at a Birmingham employer

An employer preparing several people can have the six days delivered at its own site. A structural fabricator might run the whole group on D1.1 using its own fillet and groove welds and connection details; an outage contractor might send most people to the ASME book; a mill maintenance contractor might use repair welds and hardfacing samples from its own jobs to sharpen the practical day. The company's own gauges are used throughout, so the measurement drills match what inspectors accept on the floor. Dates can be fitted around outages and project peaks. Every candidate still applies to AWS individually and meets the experience and vision rules personally.

One-to-one: online or in person

One-to-one is for the candidate who wants a tutor rather than a plan: an engineer moving into a quality role, a long-time welder who has not taken a written exam in years, or someone who needs to retake one part. It means six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, held online or in person at a location agreed when booking. The outline is unchanged, but the hours go where you need them, often symbols, fabrication math and finding answers quickly in the code book.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS sets the experience you need by your level of education: a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology means one year, completed vocational courses four, a high school diploma five, and less schooling more. The national course page has the complete table, and AWS decides what counts as welding-related work. AWS also requires its Visual Acuity Record, showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without corrective lenses, and a color perception test, completed by a qualified practitioner within the period AWS allows before the exam. If you are short of the years, the CAWI credential lets you work under a CWI while you build them. The CWI requirements and career guide goes into more detail.

After the CWI: Birmingham career paths

A CWI is valid for nine years, with AWS renewals due at the third and sixth years. In Birmingham, fabrication and construction inspectors often add code endorsements or move toward the AWS Senior CWI (see the SCWI pathway), and some go on to run welding quality programs for manufacturers or contractors.

Nondestructive testing is a natural addition, especially magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing for structural steel and power plant work. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its NDT personnel through its written practice once training and method experience are complete, and Atlantis provides that training: see NDT training in Birmingham, VT Level 2, MT Level 2 and UT Level 2. The CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II comparison sets the credentials side by side, and Practical NDT in Birmingham describes simulator-based practice. For local services, see ultrasonic testing in Birmingham, magnetic particle testing in Birmingham, MT for structural steel and ASME audit support in Birmingham.

Nearby CWI pages, and a quote

Candidates elsewhere in the Southeast can compare the CWI exam prep pages for Atlanta, Nashville, Memphis and Mobile.

For a quote, tell us how many candidates you have, which format suits each (corporate, online or one-to-one), the code book each plans to take, and a summary of their education and welding experience. For delivery at your site, add the address, the gauges and sample welds available, and any outage or project dates to avoid. Fees are not listed here; Atlantis gives a quote on request through the Birmingham CWI quote request.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Birmingham?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Birmingham; the offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. You can study online with an instructor answering questions, have your employer host the six days at its facility, or book one-to-one sessions online or in person. See the course outline.

faq.q: Who certifies me as a CWI?
faq.a: AWS administers the examination, rules on eligibility and issues the certification. Atlantis helps you prepare, has no access to exam content, and its course is not approved or endorsed by AWS.

faq.q: Which Part C code suits structural steel and fabrication work in Birmingham?
faq.a: AWS D1.1, the structural welding code for steel. It matches most fabrication shop, mill and building project work around the city. See AWS D1.1.

faq.q: I work on power plant or nuclear outages. Which book should I choose?
faq.a: The ASME package, which pairs Section IX with the B31.1 and B31.3 piping codes. Section III and Section XI are not Part C options, but the ASME package is the closest match to that work.

faq.q: Where do Birmingham candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based tests at Prometric centers, booked with the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter. Part B, the practical, is run by AWS at its own seminar and examination locations, which may mean travelling.

faq.q: Can a steel fabricator or mill contractor have the six days delivered at its plant?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery brings the six days to your facility, uses your own gauges and welds, and can be scheduled around outages or project peaks. Request a quote.

faq.q: Can one-to-one sessions be in person?
faq.a: Yes. One-to-one gives a single candidate six days of sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

faq.q: Are the practice questions copied from AWS exams?
faq.a: No. Every question is written by Atlantis from the AWS topic lists, and Atlantis has no access to the examination or its question bank.

faq.q: Does welding training at Jefferson State or Lawson State count toward eligibility?
faq.a: Completed trade or vocational courses can lower the experience AWS requires, but AWS decides which education level applies to you. Neither college is connected with the Atlantis course.

faq.q: What NDT training can I add after the CWI?
faq.a: Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT; your employer then certifies you under its written practice. See NDT training in Birmingham.
